title: Formnext Toolchangers, QIDI Q3D & G-Flex PETG
subtitle: This week in 3D printing news

topics.title: Formnext Was a Toolchanger Show
topics.description: Elegoo and Phaetus both showed toolchangers in Frankfurt this week, next to Bambu's H3C and two Kickstarter machines

slides.heading: Formnext Was a Toolchanger Show
slides.body: Formnext ran in Frankfurt this week (November 17–20). Walk the hobby halls and almost every big booth had a printer that swaps whole toolheads.
bullets: Elegoo Centauri X Ultra: four print heads, Elegoo's first toolchanger
Phaetus Hydra: the hotend company's own toolhead-switching system
Bambu H3C, AXILOOP MC8 (eight heads) and Co Print Quadro on show too
QIDI went a different way: two nozzles and a hot chamber (next topic)

slides.heading: Elegoo's Toolchanger, Up Close
slides.body: The Next Layer, November 17. A first look at the Centauri X Ultra on the show floor.

slides.heading: Centauri X Ultra: What We Know
bullets: Four independent print heads, about 5 seconds per swap
256 mm cube, same as the Centauri Carbon 2
Up to 20 colors with Elegoo's AFS unit
350 °C nozzles, 120 °C bed, 500 mm/s
Side boxes hold four spools and dry them at 65 °C
No price, no date. Specs are from the booth panel and may change

slides.heading: Phaetus Hydra
slides.body: The Next Layer, November 17. The hotend maker's own toolhead-switching system, with 1-second swaps claimed. Kit or full printer, price, date: not announced yet.

topics.title: QIDI Q3D: Two Nozzles, a Hot Chamber
topics.description: QIDI's new $599 dual-nozzle printer with a 70 °C heated chamber. I think it's the right direction for QIDI

slides.heading: QIDI Q3D: Two Nozzles, a Hot Chamber
slides.body: Launched at Formnext. I think this is the right direction for QIDI. Image: QIDI.

slides.heading: Why I Like the Direction
bullets: Two hotends, each with its own nozzle and filament path
Swap between two materials with much less purging (QIDI's claim)
70 °C heated chamber for nylon, ABS and carbon fiber
QIDI is building on what it's known for: hot, enclosed machines for tough filaments
Add the QIDI Box for multicolor on top

slides.heading: The Numbers
bullets: $599, or $749 with the QIDI Box
260 mm cube, 350 °C nozzle, 120 °C bed
CoreXY, linear rail on X, up to 600 mm/s
Bed leveling with an eddy-current sensor in the hotend
HEPA and carbon filter built in

slides.heading: Before You Pre-Order
bullets: QIDI says "pay $30, save $100". The checkout total is $529, so $70 off list
The $30 deposit is refundable
Ships about 3 months after you pay in full, so around February
No hands-on reviews yet
How the two nozzles work with the QIDI Box isn't spelled out yet

topics.title: More From Formnext
topics.description: Prusa's self-hosted printer manager, Snapmaker's color mixing, Elegoo's self-refilling resin printer, a desktop CNC that cuts steel

slides.heading: More From Formnext
bullets: Prusa Connect Local: Prusa's printer manager on your own Pi or PC, no cloud
Works with Prusa and Klipper printers. Free for personal use and small shops, public beta
Snapmaker: a top cover for the U1 and a "Full Spectrum" color-mixing filament bundle
Elegoo Saturn 5 Ultra: a resin printer that refills itself, early 2027

slides.heading: Also on the Show Floor
bullets: Makera A1S: a desktop CNC that cuts steel. $2,599 pre-order through December 4, ships January
Lynxel LB1 and LC1: resin printers for very thick resins, LC1 in full color. Kickstarter in December
Prusa previewed a rugged printer for field work
Creality: new Raptor Pro Max scanner
Bambu: no new printer, just the H3C, R1 laser and Bambu Circle

topics.title: Polymaker G-Flex: PETG That Bends
topics.description: Polymaker's new PETG and TPU blend, $21.99 a kilo. Plus Polymaker is now on the shelf at Target

slides.heading: Polymaker G-Flex: PETG That Bends
slides.body: Polymaker's new PETG and TPU blend. It bends like TPU and prints like PETG. Think snap-fits, hinges, cosplay and drone parts.
bullets: $21.99 per kilo, 1.75 mm
"No break" in impact tests, both flat and upright (Polymaker's test)
Up to 300 mm/s, and it runs through an AMS or CFS
230–240 °C nozzle, 70 °C bed
Six colors now, four more coming

slides.heading: Polymaker Is at Target Now
bullets: Polymaker filament is on the shelf at select Target stores
Panchroma PLA colors, including a new Tri Matte
Polymaker hasn't said which stores or what it costs
Seen it at a Target near you? Tell us in Discord

topics.title: Perforated Prints: Peel Off the Top
topics.description: Rau Studio's trick: print one layer of dots so the top of a part tears off cleanly

slides.heading: Perforated Prints: Peel Off the Top
slides.body: Rau Studio, November 14. A layer of printed dots works like paper perforation: the part looks solid, but the top peels off clean. No files yet.

topics.title: Stow P1: A Printer That Folds Flat
topics.description: A battery-powered printer that folds down to the size of a big book. Files on GitHub

slides.heading: Stow P1: A Printer That Folds Flat
slides.body: Fits in a backpack. Image: gao.lab (CC BY-NC-SA).

slides.heading: How It Folds
bullets: Folds to about 300 × 300 × 80 mm, roughly a big book
Opens to about 180 × 200 × 175 mm of build space
A scissor lift is the Z axis. Klipper turns its curve into straight Z moves
Runs on its own 6S battery or a 24 V supply
Mostly printed parts. CAD, parts list and firmware are all on GitHub
V1 has no heated bed or enclosure. Non-commercial license: no selling kits

topics.title: Robotics Corner: A Solar Robot Jellyfish
topics.description: A jellyfish that lives on the tank's light, UC San Diego's printed soft robot at 4.7 m/s, and a robot dog that flies

slides.heading: Robotics Corner: A Solar Robot Jellyfish
slides.body: Robert Skinner, November 15. Three years in the making. It sinks, charges from the tank lights, then pulses back up.

slides.heading: How the Jellyfish Works
bullets: A store-then-burst trick from BEAM robotics, with an ATtiny85 deciding when to fire
A saw-tooth cam pushes brass rods out under a 3D-printed silicone skin
The skin springs back and squeezes water out, like a real jellyfish
Snail cams and nautilus gears failed first. He shows them all
No files. He's planning a whole tank of solar robots

slides.heading: A Printed Soft Robot at 4.7 m/s
slides.body: UC San Diego, Science Robotics, November 18. Printed in one piece, no electronics: compressed air drives it at 4.72 m/s, and it swims. Still tethered to a compressor.

slides.heading: Sesame Drone: Now With Files
bullets: Dorian Todd's Sesame robot folds its legs into propeller arms
Walks, flies, lands, walks away
Printed carbon-fiber nylon parts take the thrust
New this week: hardware files and STLs on GitHub, November 14 (Apache-2.0)

topics.title: AI Corner: A Robot Brain Trained in Sim
topics.description: MIT's PEAR learned robots in simulation only, Google sets up an SO-101 from chat, Praxis-1 runs on the SO-101

slides.heading: AI Corner: A Robot Brain Trained in Sim
bullets: PEAR: an open 27B model from MIT, Berkeley, UC San Diego and NVIDIA
Trained only in simulation, with zero real-world demos
60% success on a real two-arm robot, up from 0% before training
Apache-2.0, and it ships an SO-101 station
Slow for now: seconds of thinking per move. No SO-101 results yet

slides.heading: Google Sets Up an SO-101 From Chat
bullets: New Gemini 4 Hydrogen model for robotics, November 17
Free Antigravity plugin installs LeRobot and calibrates an SO-101
One prompt and the arm waves. Simulation built in
Needs a paid Google AI Pro or Ultra plan

slides.heading: Praxis-1 Now Runs on the SO-101
bullets: Last week's AI Corner: Runway's open robot model
Now with an SO-101 checkpoint and a LeRobot client
Trained on about 1,070 hours of community SO-100 and SO-101 data
Apache-2.0. Aimed at a 32 GB RTX 5090

slides.heading: A Tiny Model That Makes Real Parts
bullets: smoothstone: a 1.7B model running on a regular CPU
It never writes geometry. It picks a tested OpenSCAD recipe and fills in the sizes
39 of 40 blind requests right
Writing OpenSCAD itself: 0 of 15
Free and open source (MIT)

slides.heading: Free AI Failure Detection for Farms
bullets: Printago spots spaghetti on camera, with OctoEverywhere, and pauses the printer
Free on every plan until 2027
New MCP server: Claude or ChatGPT can queue jobs and tell you which beds to clear

topics.title: Quick Tip: Two-Color Ornaments, One Nozzle
topics.description: No AMS? Add a color change partway up and swap the filament yourself

slides.heading: Quick Tip: Two-Color Ornaments, One Nozzle
slides.body: No AMS? You can still print a two-color ornament. Swap the filament partway up.
bullets: In the slicer preview, drag the layer slider to where the color should change
Add a color change or a pause on that layer
PrusaSlicer, OrcaSlicer and Bambu Studio all have it on the slider
The printer stops, you swap filament, it carries on

slides.heading: Make It Look Good
bullets: Design it in layers: a flat base color, then raised text or a star on top
Put the change on the first layer of the raised part
Push the new filament through until the color runs clean
Stay close. The printer waits for you
Same trick drops in a magnet or a nut for the hanging loop
